title: 'barroso_std'
description: 'Standardize Biodiversity Records Across Multiple Fields'

```{r}
#| eval: false
barRoso::barroso_std()
```

### Description

A wrapper function that performs integrated cleaning and standardization of
biodiversity collection records using the `barRoso` package. This includes
harmonizing taxonomic, geographic, collector, and type status information,
as well as flagging or removing unvouchered and duplicate specimens. Determiner
names in `identifiedBy` are standardized with the same rules of collector names.

### Details

This function orchestrates several std_* functions from the `barRoso`
package to clean records from virtual herbaria and biodiversity portals. It
handles multilingual field names, missing data, inconsistent formatting,
and dataset chunking for large inputs. The function also detects and optionally
removes duplicate records and specimens lacking voucher information.

**The same collector written in other ways**

After standardizing, the same collector can still be written in other ways, e.g.
`"L. Queiroz"` and `"L. P. Queiroz"`, which may be two people with the same
collector number by chance, e.g. Luis Queiroz and Luciano Paganucci de Queiroz. So,
with `match_collectors = TRUE`, a deep search is made across the whole data (not in
chunks) for records with the same first initial, surname and collector number, but
written in other ways. Compound surnames are compared in the same form, e.g.
`"A. Delgado-Salinas"`, `"A. Delgado Salinas"` and `"A. D. Salinas"` all as initials
A D and surname `Salinas`. A record gets the most complete name (with more
initials, then the longest, e.g. `"A. Delgado-Salinas"`) only when:

- its initials are among those of the complete name, with the same first initial, e.g. `"L."` in `"L. P."`, but not `"L. M."` in `"L. P."`;
- it has the same date (day, month and year) or the same municipality of a record with the complete name, which shows that they are the same collection;
- when several complete names fit, the one that agrees the most with the record is chosen, with 4 points for the same full date, 2 for the same year and month, 1 for the same year and 1 for the same municipality, e.g. `"E. H. A. Rodrigues"` of the same date and municipality rather than `"E. M. A. Rodrigues"` of the same municipality, for `"E. A. Rodrigues"`. When different people agree as much, e.g. `"L. Queiroz"` with `"L. P. Queiroz"` and `"L. M. Queiroz"`, the record is kept.

**Updating a database**

With `database`, new downloads are added to a database already standardized by
`barroso_std()`, e.g. after duplicates were removed and records were corrected by
hand, without standardizing it again and without losing the corrections:

1. New records already in the database are removed by their identifiers, the same `occurrenceID` (or `gbifID`, when present) of the same `datasource`.
2. The other new records are standardized as usual.
3. New records whose herbarium and catalog number, e.g. `"MO 2839102"`, are in the database, in `catalogNumber` or among the duplicates of its records (`duplicateCatalogNumbers`), are removed, as they are the same herbarium sheet.
4. Duplicates are flagged (and removed, with `rm_duplicates = TRUE`) among the new records.
5. New records that are duplicates of a record of the database (same collector and number) are added to its duplicate columns, e.g. their herbaria and catalog numbers to `duplicateCollectionCodes` and `duplicateCatalogNumbers`, and, with `rm_duplicates = TRUE`, removed. A different name sets `identificationConflict`, but the name of the database is kept.

The records of the database are not changed, except their duplicate columns in
step 5. The result has the records of the database and the new records, with the
column `newRecord` (`TRUE` for the new records), so that they can be checked.

The final data frame is sorted by species, `recordedBy` and `recordNumber`. All
records of a block of duplicates stay together under the name of the block, which
is the most frequent name among its duplicates. For example, a duplicate identified
as `"Ormosia ruddiana"` goes together with its three duplicates identified as
`"Ormosia amazonica"`, in the place of the latter species.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| ... | Input data frame containing raw biodiversity records. |
| unvouchered | Logical; if `TRUE`, remove records of wood, seed, fruit, pollen and spirit collections (e.g. `"INPAw"`, `"INPA-Carpoteca"`), and observations without a specimen (`basisOfRecord` like `"HUMAN_OBSERVATION"`) (default: `TRUE`). |
| delunkcoll | Logical; if `TRUE`, removes records with unknown or missing collectors (default: `FALSE`). |
| flag_missid | Reserved for future use. Currently not implemented. |
| flag_duplicates | Logical; if `TRUE`, flags duplicates with a logical column (default: `TRUE`). |
| rm_duplicates | Logical; if `TRUE`, removes duplicate specimens (default: `FALSE`). |
| specialists | Optional data frame with the columns `specialist` and `taxon` (a family, genus or species of expertise), e.g. `data.frame(specialist = "D. B. O. S. Cardoso", taxon = "Leguminosae")`, whose identifications are preferred when removing duplicates with conflicting identifications. See `barroso_flag_duplicates()` (default: `NULL`). |
| flag_specialists | Logical; if `TRUE`, the records identified by the `specialists` are flagged in the columns `specialistIdentification`, `specialistName` and `specialistEvidence`, before duplicates are removed, so that a record kept from a block of duplicates is flagged when one of its duplicates with the same name was identified by a specialist. See `barroso_flag_specialists()` (default: `FALSE`). |
| rm_tied_conflicts | Logical; with `rm_duplicates = TRUE`, if `TRUE`, blocks of duplicates whose conflicting names are equally frequent are removed entirely; if `FALSE`, all their records are kept. See `barroso_flag_duplicates()` (default: `FALSE`). |
| database | Optional data frame, or path to an .xlsx, .csv or .rds file, with records already standardized by `barroso_std()`, to which the new records are added. See Details (default: `NULL`). |
| match_collectors | Logical; if `TRUE`, the same collector written in other ways across the whole data, e.g. `"L. Queiroz"` and `"L. P. Queiroz"`, or `"A. D. Salinas"`, `"A. Delgado Salinas"` and `"A. Delgado-Salinas"`, gets the most complete name, before duplicates are found. See Details (default: `TRUE`). |
| index_herbariorum | Logical; if `TRUE`, checks collection codes against the API of Index Herbariorum, always keeping the original codes. See `std_collection()`. Use `FALSE` to work offline (default: `TRUE`). |
| colname_recordedBy | Column name for collector names. |
| colname_recordNumber | Column name for collector number. |
| colname_identifiedBy | Column name for determiner names. The column is standardized with `std_identifiedBy()` only when present in the data. |
| colname_continent | Column name for continent. |
| colname_country | Column name for country. |
| colname_stateProvince | Column name for state/province. |
| colname_county | Column name for county. |
| colname_municipality | Column name for municipality. |
| colname_locality | Column name for locality. |
| colname_collectionCode | Column name for collection code. |
| colname_institutionCode | Column name for institution code. |
| colname_typeStatus | Column name for type status. |
| colname_family | Column name for family. |
| colname_genus | Column name for genus. |
| colname_specificEpithet | Column name for specific epithet. |
| rm_original_column | Logical; if `TRUE`, remove original columns after standardization, except that of collection codes when `index_herbariorum = TRUE`. |
| std_collection | Logical; if `FALSE`, the function will not standardize the collection codes according to Index Herbariorum. |

### Value

A fully cleaned and standardized data frame ready for downstream reconciliation,
duplicate handling, and label generation.

### Examples

```r
df <- read.csv("raw_herbarium_data.csv")
df_std <- barroso_std(df,
                      colname_country = "pais",
                      colname_stateProvince = "estado",
                      rm_duplicates = TRUE)
```
